title: SA 315 - Identifying and Assessing the Risks of Material Misstatement
description: Comprehensive CA Final Audit MCQs covering SA 315 Identifying and Assessing the Risks of Material Misstatement Through Understanding the Entity and Its Environment.

questions.category: SA 315 - Audit Risk and Its Components
questions.question:
Assertion (A): The objective of the statutory auditor under the Standards on Auditing is to reduce audit risk to zero so as to provide absolute assurance to the users of financial statements.

Reason (R): Audit risk is a function of the risks of material misstatement (inherent risk and control risk) and detection risk, and because inherent limitations of internal control and auditing always exist, audit risk can only be reduced to an acceptably low level, not to zero.

In the light of SA 315 and basic audit principles, which of the following is correct?
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are correct, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is incorrect because the auditor is neither required nor able to reduce audit risk to zero; an audit does not provide absolute assurance due to the inherent limitations of internal control and auditing. The objective of the auditor under SA 315 and general audit principles is to reduce audit risk to an acceptably low level. Reason (R) is correct as it accurately defines Audit Risk as the risk that the auditor expresses an inappropriate opinion when financial statements are materially misstated, which is a product of ROMM and Detection Risk (Audit Risk = ROMM × Detection Risk), and explains why inherent limitations prevent eliminating audit risk entirely.

questions.category: SA 315 - Audit Risk and Its Components
questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the interrelationship among the components of Audit Risk:

Statement 1: Risk of Material Misstatement (ROMM) consists of Inherent Risk and Control Risk, representing the anticipated risk that material misstatement may exist in financial statements prior to audit (ROMM = Inherent Risk × Control Risk).
Statement 2: Inherent Risk is the susceptibility of an assertion about a class of transaction, account balance, or disclosure (CAD) towards misstatements before considering any related internal controls.
Statement 3: Control Risk is the risk that an entity's internal control system will not prevent, or detect and correct, a material misstatement on a timely basis, or that such control will be missing.
Statement 4: Detection Risk is directly proportional to ROMM, meaning that if the auditor assesses ROMM as high, the auditor sets an acceptably higher detection risk to conserve audit effort.

Which of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements 1, 2, and 3 are correct. ROMM is the anticipated risk that financial statements are materially misstated prior to audit, comprising Inherent Risk and Control Risk (ROMM = Inherent Risk × Control Risk). Inherent Risk relates to the susceptibility of assertions about CAD towards misstatements arising from entity objectives, operations, industry, regulation, size, and complexity. Control Risk represents the risk that internal controls fail to prevent, detect, or correct material misstatements timely. Statement 4 is incorrect because ROMM is inversely related to Detection Risk: when ROMM is high, the auditor must perform more extensive testing to reduce detection risk to an acceptably low level.

questions.category: SA 315 - Audit Risk and Its Components
questions.question:
Case Study 1:
CA. Rohan is appointed as the statutory auditor of Nexa Finserve Ltd., a fast-growing non-banking financial company. During initial planning, Rohan notes that the company deals in complex derivative instruments and operates in an intensely volatile regulatory environment. At the same time, the company's internal control system has well-documented SOPs, automated three-way matching, and an active audit committee. However, Rohan assumes that because the internal controls appear well-designed, Control Risk can be assessed as 'Nil' or 'Zero', thereby eliminating the risk of material misstatement prior to audit.

Evaluate CA. Rohan's assessment of Control Risk in accordance with SA 315:
options: Rohan's assessment is correct because automated systems and an active audit committee eliminate control failures.
Rohan's assessment is incorrect because some control risk will always exist due to the inherent limitations of any internal control system.
Rohan's assessment is correct provided he obtains a written representation from management confirming zero control deficiencies during the year.
Rohan's assessment is incorrect solely because derivative instruments are legally prohibited from being covered by internal controls.
questions.explanation: Under SA 315, some control risk will always exist because of the inherent limitations of any internal control system (such as human judgment errors, management override, collusion, or system breakdowns). Even the most sophisticated internal control framework cannot guarantee that all misstatements will be prevented, or detected and corrected, on a timely basis. Therefore, an auditor can never assess control risk as 'Zero' or 'Nil'. Rohan's assumption violates this fundamental premise of SA 315.

questions.category: SA 315 - Audit Risk and Its Components
questions.question:
Case Study 1:
CA. Rohan is appointed as the statutory auditor of Nexa Finserve Ltd., a fast-growing non-banking financial company. During initial planning, Rohan notes that the company deals in complex derivative instruments and operates in an intensely volatile regulatory environment. At the same time, the company's internal control system has well-documented SOPs, automated three-way matching, and an active audit committee. However, Rohan assumes that because the internal controls appear well-designed, Control Risk can be assessed as 'Nil' or 'Zero', thereby eliminating the risk of material misstatement prior to audit.

Suppose that upon proper evaluation, CA. Rohan assesses the Risk of Material Misstatement (ROMM) for derivative valuations as 'High'. In accordance with the inverse relationship between ROMM and Detection Risk under SA 315, what is the appropriate audit response regarding Detection Risk and substantive testing?
options: Rohan should accept a higher Detection Risk and reduce the extent of detailed substantive testing.
Rohan should maintain an unchanged Detection Risk because Detection Risk is independent of the entity's ROMM.
Rohan must perform more extensive checking and substantive audit procedures to achieve a lower Detection Risk, thereby keeping overall Audit Risk at an acceptably low level.
Rohan should issue a qualified audit opinion immediately without performing any substantive procedures since ROMM is high.
questions.explanation: SA 315 establishes that ROMM is inversely related to Detection Risk. If the auditor assesses ROMM as high, the auditor cannot tolerate a high detection risk; the auditor must do more checking (increasing the nature, timing, and extent of audit procedures) to drive Detection Risk down to a low level. This ensures that the overall Audit Risk (Audit Risk = ROMM × Detection Risk) remains at an acceptably low level. Reducing substantive checking or accepting a high detection risk when ROMM is high would result in an unacceptably high audit risk.

questions.question:
Which of the following combinations of audit procedures are explicitly recognized under SA 315 as Risk Assessment Procedures for understanding the entity and its environment (to assess Inherent Risk and Control Risk)?

(i) Inquiries of management and others within the entity
(ii) Observation of entity operations and internal control processes
(iii) Analytical procedures applied to financial and non-financial data
(iv) External circularization and confirmation of all trade receivables balances
questions.explanation: SA 315 explicitly specifies that risk assessment procedures for obtaining an understanding of the entity and its environment, including its internal control, comprise inquiries (of management and others), observation, and analytical procedures (with inquiries and observation specifically highlighted for understanding internal control). External confirmation of trade receivables is a substantive procedure (test of details) under SA 505 / SA 330, not a risk assessment procedure for obtaining business understanding under SA 315.

questions.question:
Case Study 2:
CA. Radhika is conducting the statutory audit of BluePeak Pharma Ltd., a listed enterprise manufacturing active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs). During the risk assessment stage to assess Inherent Risk under SA 315, Radhika designs procedures to obtain knowledge of the business across various aspects of the entity and its environment.

Which of the following areas are required to be understood by CA. Radhika under SA 315 to assess Inherent Risk?

1. Relevant industry, regulatory, and other external factors.
2. Nature of the entity, including its operations, type of investments, ownership and governance structure, and the way in which the entity is financed.
3. Entity's selection and application of accounting policies.
4. Entity's objectives and strategies, and related business risks.
5. Measurement and review of the entity's financial performance.
questions.explanation: Under SA 315, for assessing Inherent Risk, the auditor shall obtain an understanding of: (1) Relevant industry, regulatory & other external factors; (2) Nature of entity including operations, investments, ownership & governance structure, and financing; (3) Entity's selection & application of accounting policies; (4) Entity's objectives & strategies & related business risks; and (5) Measurement & review of entity's financial performance. All five listed items are explicitly mandated by SA 315.

questions.question:
Case Study 2:
CA. Radhika is conducting the statutory audit of BluePeak Pharma Ltd., a listed enterprise manufacturing active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs). During the risk assessment stage to assess Inherent Risk under SA 315, Radhika designs procedures to obtain knowledge of the business across various aspects of the entity and its environment.

While evaluating the 'Nature of the entity', Radhika examines BluePeak Pharma's recent aggressive acquisition of an overseas research lab funded 85% through high-yield debt notes, as well as its complex cross-holding ownership structure. Under SA 315, these specific inquiries directly relate to understanding which component of the entity?

Statement 1: The entity's type of investments.
Statement 2: The entity's ownership and governance structure.
Statement 3: The way in which the entity is financed.
Statement 4: The internal control procedures over journal entries.
questions.explanation: Under SA 315, the auditor's understanding of the 'nature of the entity' specifically includes its operations, its type of investments (such as the acquisition of the overseas research lab), its ownership and governance structure (such as the cross-holding structure), and the way in which the entity is financed (such as funding 85% via high-yield debt notes). Statement 4 relates to entity internal controls / control risk procedures rather than the inherent nature of the entity.

questions.question: For obtaining an understanding of the entity's internal control to assess Control Risk under SA 315, what specific risk assessment procedures is the auditor required to conduct?
options: Inspection of statutory register of members only
questions.explanation: According to SA 315, for assessing Control Risk, the auditor is required to understand the entity's internal control by conducting inquiries and observation. While analytical procedures and inquiry are also used for broader inherent risk and business understanding, the specific risk assessment procedures for understanding the internal control system focus on inquiries of entity personnel and observation of the application of controls.

questions.question:
Under SA 315, 'Assertions' are defined as representations by management, explicit or otherwise, that are embodied in the financial statements. In which of the following categories are these representations categorized for the purpose of assessing the risk of material misstatement?

(i) Classes of transactions and events for the period under audit
(ii) Account balances at the period end
(iii) Presentation and disclosure
(iv) Budgetary forecasts and projections for future periods
questions.explanation: SA 315 defines assertions as representations by management embodied in the financial statements about: (i) classes of transactions and events for the period under audit, (ii) account balances at the period end, and (iii) presentation and disclosure. Budgetary forecasts and future projections are not representations embodied in historical financial statements under SA 315.

questions.question:
Case Study 3:
During the audit of Alpha Motors Ltd., CA. Pradeep is evaluating management's assertions regarding the revenue cycle (classes of transactions and events during the year). 

Match the specific audit situation described in Column I with the relevant Assertion about classes of transactions in Column II:

Column I (Audit Situation)
A. Fictitious sales invoices were recorded without any shipment of goods.
B. Valid sales made on 30th March were recorded on 3rd April of the subsequent financial year.
C. Repair expenses of machinery were capitalized as plant & equipment instead of being charged to revenue.
D. Goods dispatched were omitted from being billed and recorded in the sales journal.

Column II (Assertion under SA 315)
1. Completeness
2. Occurrence
3. Cut-off
4. Classification
questions.explanation: The assertions about classes of transactions under SA 315 are: (A) Fictitious sales recorded without shipment violates 'Occurrence' (transactions recorded did not occur) -> 2; (B) Recording 30th March sales on 3rd April violates 'Cut-off' (transactions recorded in the correct accounting period) -> 3; (C) Capitalizing repairs instead of expensing relates to 'Classification' (recorded in proper accounts) -> 4; (D) Omitting dispatches from sales journal violates 'Completeness' (all transactions that should have been recorded have been recorded) -> 1. Thus, the correct match is A-2, B-3, C-4, D-1.

questions.question: Which of the following sets of assertions strictly relates to 'Account Balances' at the period end under SA 315?
options: Occurrence, Completeness, Accuracy, Cut-off, and Classification
Existence, Completeness, Rights & Obligations, and Valuation & Allocation
Occurrence, Rights & Obligations, Completeness, Classification & Understandability, and Accuracy & Valuation
questions.explanation: SA 315 explicitly classifies assertions into three categories. Assertions about account balances at period end are: (1) Existence, (2) Completeness, (3) Rights & Obligations, and (4) Valuation & Allocation. Occurrence and Cut-off are assertions about classes of transactions, whereas Classification & Understandability is an assertion about presentation and disclosure.

questions.question:
Case Study 4:
Sunlit Energy Ltd. has pledged its primary solar plant assets against a term loan availed from an infrastructure fund. In the notes to the financial statements, management has omitted the disclosure of the charge created on the solar plant and has also grouped long-term borrowings as current trade payables.

Which assertions regarding 'Presentation and Disclosure' under SA 315 are directly violated by Sunlit Energy Ltd.?
options: Completeness, Rights & Obligations, and Classification & Understandability
questions.explanation: Under SA 315, assertions about presentation and disclosure include: Occurrence and Rights & Obligations, Completeness, Classification & Understandability, and Accuracy & Valuation. Pledging an asset affects Rights & Obligations and its non-disclosure violates Completeness of disclosures. Grouping long-term borrowings under current trade payables violates Classification & Understandability. Cut-off is an assertion relating to classes of transactions, not presentation and disclosure.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Under SA 315, the auditor is required to identify and assess the risks of material misstatement at two levels: the financial statement level, and the assertion level for classes of transactions, account balances, and disclosures (CAD).

Reason (R): Risks of material misstatement at the financial statement level refer to risks that relate pervasively to the financial statements as a whole and potentially affect many assertions, whereas risks at the assertion level help determine the nature, timing, and extent of further audit procedures at the CAD level.

In the light of SA 315, which of the following is correct?
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are correct, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
questions.explanation: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct, and (R) correctly explains (A). SA 315 explicitly mandates that the auditor shall identify and assess ROMM at both: (1) the financial statement level, and (2) the assertion level for classes of transactions, account balances, and disclosures. The distinction is fundamental: financial statement level risks relate pervasively to the financial statements as a whole (such as management override of controls or deficient control environment) and potentially affect multiple assertions, whereas assertion-level risks are specific to particular CAD and guide the design of specific further audit procedures.

questions.category: SA 315 - Considerations of Auditor to Assess ROMM
questions.question:
Case Study 5:
CA. Aniket is the statutory auditor of Zenith Apparel Ltd. In order to assess the risks of material misstatement in accordance with SA 315, Aniket establishes a systematic four-step risk assessment approach.

Arrange the following four considerations of the auditor to assess ROMM under SA 315 in their logical operational sequence:

Step 1: Relate the identified risks to what can go wrong at the assertion level.
Step 2: Identify risks including relevant controls throughout the process of obtaining an understanding of the entity and its environment by considering classes of transactions, account balances, and disclosures.
Step 3: Consider the likelihood of misstatement, including the possibility of multiple misstatements, and whether the potential misstatement is of a magnitude that could result in a material misstatement.
Step 4: Assess the identified risks and evaluate whether they relate more pervasively to the financial statements as a whole and potentially affect many assertions.
questions.explanation: SA 315 lays down the four considerations for assessing ROMM: (1) Identify risks throughout the process of obtaining an understanding of the entity and its environment, by considering classes of transactions, account balances, and disclosures (Step 2); (2) Assess the identified risks and evaluate whether they relate more pervasively to the financial statements as a whole and potentially affect many assertions (Step 4); (3) Relate the identified risks to what can go wrong at the assertion level (Step 1); and (4) Consider the likelihood of misstatement, including possibility of multiple misstatements, and whether potential misstatement is of a magnitude that could result in material misstatement (Step 3). The logical sequence is 2 -> 4 -> 1 -> 3.

questions.category: SA 315 - Considerations of Auditor to Assess ROMM
questions.question:
Case Study 5:
CA. Aniket is the statutory auditor of Zenith Apparel Ltd. In order to assess the risks of material misstatement in accordance with SA 315, Aniket establishes a systematic four-step risk assessment approach.

While evaluating identified risks, Aniket observes that the entity's management compensation is heavily tied to EBITDA targets, and the Chief Financial Officer lacks basic accounting competence. Aniket determines that these factors could result in widespread bias affecting revenue recognition, inventory valuation, and liability provisions across the entire entity.

Under SA 315, how should CA. Aniket classify and evaluate this risk?
options: As an isolated risk relating solely to the assertion of 'Cut-off' in payroll expenses.
As a risk that relates pervasively to the financial statements as a whole and potentially affects many assertions (Financial Statement Level Risk).
As a non-audit operational risk that does not require any assessment under SA 315.
As a Detection Risk arising exclusively from the auditor's lack of familiarity with the apparel industry.
questions.explanation: Under SA 315, risks that arise from pervasive weaknesses such as management integrity concerns, aggressive incentive structures, or an incompetent financial leadership do not relate to a single isolated assertion; they relate pervasively to the financial statements as a whole and potentially affect many assertions across multiple account balances and transaction streams. Such risks are evaluated at the Financial Statement level.

questions.question:
Which of the following factors are explicitly required to be considered by the auditor under SA 315 to determine whether an identified risk is a 'Significant Risk' requiring special audit consideration?

1. Whether the risk is a risk of fraud.
2. Whether the risk is related to recent significant economic, accounting, or other developments.
3. The complexity of transactions.
4. Whether the risk involves significant transactions with related parties.
5. Whether the risk involves significant transactions that are outside the normal course of business.
questions.explanation: SA 315 explicitly lists the factors the auditor shall consider in determining whether a risk is a significant risk requiring special audit consideration: (1) Whether the risk is a risk of fraud; (2) Whether the risk is related to recent significant economic, accounting or other developments; (3) Complexity of transactions; (4) Whether the risk involves significant transactions with related parties; and (5) Whether the risk involves significant transactions that are outside the normal course of business. All 5 factors are explicitly stated in SA 315.

questions.question:
Case Study 6:
During the financial year, Regal Real Estate Ltd. entered into a major unhedged structured debt-cum-equity swap agreement worth ₹400 Crore with an entity owned by the brother of the Managing Director. The agreement involves complex variable interest derivatives and profit-sharing clauses, and is entirely outside Regal Real Estate Ltd.'s regular business of residential construction. The engagement partner, CA. Somesh, is determining whether this transaction constitutes a 'Significant Risk' under SA 315.

Which of the following statements is correct regarding CA. Somesh's determination under SA 315?
options: The transaction is a routine operational risk because real estate entities frequently execute land-for-equity swaps.

The transaction embodies multiple factors that trigger classification as a Significant Risk: it involves complexity of transactions, significant transactions with related parties, and significant transactions outside the normal course of business.
The transaction cannot be a Significant Risk unless the statutory auditor has already proven the occurrence of actual criminal fraud.
The transaction is purely a Control Risk and therefore does not require special audit consideration under SA 315.
questions.explanation: Under SA 315, in determining whether a risk is a significant risk, the auditor evaluates whether the risk involves complexity of transactions, significant transactions with related parties, and significant transactions that are outside the normal course of business. In Regal Real Estate Ltd.'s scenario, all three factors are present: a complex structured debt-equity swap, executed with a related party (MD's brother's entity), and outside the normal course of residential construction. Thus, it undeniably constitutes a Significant Risk requiring special audit consideration.

questions.question:
Case Study 6:
During the financial year, Regal Real Estate Ltd. entered into a major unhedged structured debt-cum-equity swap agreement worth ₹400 Crore with an entity owned by the brother of the Managing Director. The agreement involves complex variable interest derivatives and profit-sharing clauses, and is entirely outside Regal Real Estate Ltd.'s regular business of residential construction. The engagement partner, CA. Somesh, is determining whether this transaction constitutes a 'Significant Risk' under SA 315.

Suppose management argues that because the transaction was vetted by an external law firm, the auditor should exclude the effects of identified internal controls and not treat it as a Significant Risk. What is the fundamental principle under SA 315 regarding internal controls when determining whether a risk is a significant risk?
options: The auditor must consider internal controls first, and if controls are well-designed, the risk can never be classified as a significant risk.
In determining whether a risk is a significant risk, the auditor shall exclude the effects of identified controls related to the risk (assessing the inherent susceptibility to misstatement).
The auditor is required to classify transactions as significant risks only if internal controls are completely absent in the entity.
External legal opinions automatically downgrade significant risks to routine detection risks.
questions.explanation: Under SA 315, in exercising judgment as to which risks are significant risks, the auditor shall exclude the effects of identified controls related to the risk. A significant risk is determined based on the inherent nature, complexity, magnitude, and likelihood of misstatement (e.g. fraud, related party, outside normal course) before considering mitigating controls. If the auditor factored in controls prematurely, management could mask inherently high-risk transactions behind cosmetic control descriptions.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Under SA 315, obtaining an understanding of the entity and its environment, including its internal control, is a continuous, dynamic process of gathering, updating, and analyzing information throughout the audit.

Reason (R): If during the audit, information comes to the auditor's attention that differs significantly from the information on which the initial risk assessment was based, the auditor shall revise the inherent risk or control risk, revise ROMM, and modify further planned audit procedures accordingly.

In the light of SA 315, which of the following is correct?
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are correct, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
questions.explanation: Both (A) and (R) are correct, and (R) correctly explains (A). SA 315 makes it explicit that obtaining an understanding of the entity and its environment is not an isolated one-time event performed only at the beginning of the audit, but a continuous and cumulative process of gathering, updating, and analyzing information throughout the audit engagement. When substantive procedures or new evidence reveal conditions that differ significantly from those initially assumed (e.g., higher error rates or control failures), the auditor must revise the assessed Inherent Risk or Control Risk (and consequently ROMM) and modify the planned nature, timing, and extent of further audit procedures.

questions.question:
Case Study 7:
CA. Shalini is auditing TruTech Ltd. At the planning stage, she assessed Control Risk over procurement as 'Low' based on management's inquiry and walk-through of the automated ERP system. However, during substantive testing of purchases in month eight, Shalini discovers that the procurement manager had been granted unrestricted super-user rights five months ago, allowing manual approval of vendor payments without GRN matching, resulting in several unauthorized payments.

What is the mandatory course of action for CA. Shalini under SA 315?
options: Shalini must maintain her initial risk assessment since planning parameters cannot be altered once execution begins.
Shalini shall revise the assessed Control Risk upwards, leading to a revised (higher) assessment of ROMM, and modify the nature, timing, and extent of further planned audit procedures.
Shalini should immediately withdraw from the audit engagement without performing any further verification.
Shalini should ignore the finding if management provides a verbal promise to revoke the super-user rights before the balance sheet date.
questions.explanation: SA 315 explicitly states that obtaining an understanding of internal control is a continuous process. When information comes to the auditor's attention that differs significantly from the information on which the initial risk assessment was based (such as discovery of super-user access and bypass of controls), the auditor shall revise the inherent risk or control risk, which leads to a revision in ROMM, and modify further planned audit procedures accordingly (e.g., expanding substantive tests of details over procurement).

questions.category: SA 315 - IT Environment and IT Risks to Internal Control
questions.question:
IT systems also pose specific risks to an entity's internal control. Which of the following are explicitly identified in SA 315 as examples of IT risks to an entity's internal control?

1. Reliance on systems or programs that are inaccurately processing data or processing inaccurate data.
2. Unauthorized access to data that may result in destruction of data or improper changes to data.
3. Possibility of IT personnel gaining privileges beyond those necessary to perform their assigned duties (extra access).
4. Unauthorized changes to systems or programs.
5. Failure to make necessary changes to systems or programs.
6. Inappropriate manual intervention.
7. Potential loss of data or inability to access data as required.
questions.explanation: All seven points are explicitly cited in SA 315 as specific examples of IT risks to an entity's internal control: (1) Reliance on systems/programs inaccurately processing data or processing inaccurate data; (2) Unauthorized access to data; (3) Possibility of IT personnel gaining extra access; (4) Unauthorized changes to data; (5) Unauthorized changes to systems/programs; (6) Failure to make changes to systems/programs; (7) Inappropriate manual intervention; and (8) Potential loss of data or inability to access data.

questions.category: SA 315 - IT Environment and IT Risks to Internal Control
questions.question:
Case Study 8:
CyberNet Solutions Ltd. operates an automated billing and financial reporting platform. During the IT controls review, the auditor observes the following four conditions:

Condition A: The lead system developer has administrative rights allowing direct table updates in the live production database without logging.
Condition B: The ERP system was not updated to incorporate the revised GST rate change enacted by the government, causing inaccurate tax calculations.
Condition C: The accounts manager manually overrides the system-generated exchange rates every month-end using arbitrary rates written on notepad sheets.
Condition D: Tape backup logs indicate recurring media errors for three consecutive months without offsite replication.

Match these conditions to the specific IT risks to internal control outlined in SA 315:

1. Possibility of IT personnel gaining extra access / Unauthorized changes to data
2. Failure to make necessary changes to systems or programs
3. Inappropriate manual intervention
4. Potential loss of data or inability to access data
questions.explanation: Under SA 315: Condition A represents IT personnel gaining extra access / unauthorized changes to live data (1); Condition B represents failure to make necessary changes to systems or programs in response to regulatory updates (2); Condition C represents inappropriate manual intervention overriding automated processes (3); Condition D represents potential loss of data or inability to access data due to defective backup and recovery (4). Therefore, the correct matching is A-1, B-2, C-3, D-4.

questions.category: SA 315 - IT Environment and IT Risks to Internal Control
questions.question:
Case Study 8:
CyberNet Solutions Ltd. operates an automated billing and financial reporting platform. During the IT controls review, the auditor observes that the billing software had an algorithmic logic flaw for 45 days, during which it computed discounts on gross invoice amounts before deducting returns, thereby generating flawed sales ledgers.

Which specific IT risk to internal control under SA 315 does this scenario exemplify?
options: Reliance on systems or programs that are inaccurately processing data, or processing inaccurate data
Inability to access data due to hardware failure
Unauthorized physical access by third parties to the server room
Inappropriate manual intervention by senior management
questions.explanation: SA 315 explicitly identifies 'Reliance on systems or programs that are inaccurately processing data, or that are processing inaccurate data' as a key IT risk to an entity's internal control. When a billing program contains an incorrect calculation algorithm that systematically miscalculates discounts, the entity and its financial reporting are relying on a program that is inaccurately processing data.

questions.category: SA 315 - Integrated Case Study: Risk Assessment and Assertions
questions.question:
Case Study 9:
CA. Manas is auditing Vistara Logistics Ltd. During the risk assessment process, Manas identifies the following four findings:

Finding 1: Management bonuses depend exclusively on achieving a 20% annual growth in reported net profits, creating high entity-wide pressure.
Finding 2: The company introduced a new complex revenue sharing scheme with 40 independent franchise partners, involving variable consideration and volume rebates.
Finding 3: During year-end cut-off testing, three dispatches on 31st March were billed but goods remained in the warehouse without delivery to customers.
Finding 4: The IT administrator has unchecked authority to modify financial ledger tables directly without change-management approval.

Which of the following statements correctly synthesizes the classification of these findings under SA 315?
options: Finding 1 is a Financial Statement level risk; Finding 2 is an indicator of Significant Risk; Finding 3 is an assertion-level risk relating to Occurrence/Cut-off; and Finding 4 is a specific IT risk to internal control.
Finding 1 is an Account Balance assertion risk; Finding 2 is Detection Risk; Finding 3 is a Presentation and Disclosure assertion risk; and Finding 4 is an Inherent Risk of the transport industry.
All four findings represent Detection Risk that CA. Manas can eliminate by obtaining written representations.
Finding 1 and Finding 2 are Control Risks only, while Finding 3 and Finding 4 are Inherent Risks only.
questions.explanation: Under SA 315: Finding 1 (entity-wide bonus pressure) relates pervasively to the financial statements as a whole, representing a Financial Statement level risk. Finding 2 (complex revenue sharing with partners) involves complexity and potential related party/special considerations, which are key factors in determining a Significant Risk. Finding 3 (billing without dispatch) directly impacts the assertion level for classes of transactions (Occurrence and Cut-off). Finding 4 (IT administrator direct modification access) is a classic IT risk to internal control (possibility of IT personnel gaining extra access and unauthorized changes to data).

questions.category: SA 315 - Integrated Case Study: Risk Assessment and Assertions
questions.question:
Case Study 9:
CA. Manas is auditing Vistara Logistics Ltd. During the risk assessment process, Manas identifies the following four findings:

Finding 1: Management bonuses depend exclusively on achieving a 20% annual growth in reported net profits, creating high entity-wide pressure.
Finding 2: The company introduced a new complex revenue sharing scheme with 40 independent franchise partners, involving variable consideration and volume rebates.
Finding 3: During year-end cut-off testing, three dispatches on 31st March were billed but goods remained in the warehouse without delivery to customers.
Finding 4: The IT administrator has unchecked authority to modify financial ledger tables directly without change-management approval.

In relation to Finding 3, if management included these dispatches in sales revenue for the year ended 31st March while the risks and rewards/control of goods did not pass to the customer, which assertion about classes of transactions under SA 315 is primarily breached?
questions.explanation: For classes of transactions and events, the assertion that recorded transactions and events occurred and pertain to the entity is 'Occurrence'. Recording sales when goods have not been delivered and revenue recognition criteria are not met breaches the 'Occurrence' assertion (the sale did not occur during the period). 'Existence' is an assertion about account balances at period end, 'Rights & Obligations' applies to account balances and disclosures, and 'Classification & Understandability' applies to presentation & disclosure.
